reference: Polymetallic massive sulfide, Potter Mine (Commons title)

description.lithology: Fine-grained mafic metavolcanic / chlorite schist-like rock. Colour is dark green-grey to grey with mottled green and purple-grey patches and a thin orange-brown oxidation rim along the bottom edge. Grain size is fine-grained, essentially aphanitic to very fine grained. Texture is massive to weakly foliated/sheared with sub-parallel dark streaking / lineation running roughly sub-vertical to the core axis. Fabric is weakly foliated / lineated with a sheared appearance.
description.alteration: Chloritic alteration, moderate to strong and pervasive, giving the green-grey groundmass colour; weak to moderate local oxidation / iron staining orange-brown along margins. No strong sericitic, potassic, silicified or carbonate alteration is clearly distinguishable in the photo resolution.
description.mineralization: none visible. No confidently identifiable sulfide or ore minerals can be resolved in the image; the dark band is a fine-grained rock/vein material rather than a clearly visible sulfide assemblage at this resolution.

anomalies.explanation: A prominent dark, near-black, sub-vertical to oblique vein / shear band cuts the core from top to bottom with a thin pale yellowish selvage along its margin; the feature should be checked in hand specimen for composition and for possible sulfide/carbonate content.
Thin, discontinuous pale greenish to yellowish fracture fillings / veinlets are visible throughout the core, consistent with chlorite / carbonate / secondary mineral infill; confirm in hand specimen.
